items.title: Ribbon Cutting Ceremony Held for Forsyth County Water Treatment Plant Upgrades
items.summary: Forsyth County officials held a ribbon cutting ceremony on Friday, June 12, for a recent expansion at the Forsyth County Water Treatment Plant (2255 Antioch Road) in north Forsyth. The expansion at the facility increased the peak water treatment capacity from 33 million gallons per day (MGD) to 40 MGD.

items.title: Forysth County to Cooperatively Manage Five Additional Lake Lanier Access Parks
items.summary: Forsyth County and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) have finalized a new Challenge Cost-Sharing Cooperative Management Agreement (CCSCMA) that will shift certain responsibilities from the USACE to Forsyth County for five Lake Lanier parks/water access areas previously solely managed by the USACE.

items.title: Cup of FoCo: Behind the Wheel with Access Forsyth
items.summary: Grab a cup of coffee and hop aboard with Denny, one of the friendly drivers helping keep Forsyth County moving through Access Forsyth public transportation. In this episode of Cup of FoCo, we ride along with Denny to learn more about his role, the riders he serves and what makes Access Forsyth such an important resource for the community.

items.title: Matt Schoolhouse Community Building Ribbon Cutting | May 2026
items.summary: A ribbon cutting ceremony was held at 10 a.m. on Tuesday, May 12, to celebrate the opening of the historic Matt Schoolhouse Community Building (5710 Namon Wallace Road) in northwest Forsyth County following a large-scale renovation project. items.title: Bennett Park Reopening Ribbon Cutting | April 2026
items.summary: A ribbon cutting ceremony was held at 1 p.m. on Wednesday, April 29, to celebrate the reopening of Bennett Park (5930 Burruss Mill Road) in northeast Forsyth County following a large-scale renovation project. The ceremony featured remarks from District 4 Commissioner Mendy Moore, Forsyth County Manager David McKee, Parks & Recreation Director Kirk Franz, Levi Brush with MAPP, and Keith Hightower with Hussey Gay Bell.

items.title: Cumming-Forsyth County Miracle League Celebrates 20 Years
items.summary: Forsyth County Parks & Recreation recently hosted the Cumming-Forsyth Miracle League at Lanierland Park for a special celebration marking the organization’s 20th anniversary. Hear more about the Miracle League of Cumming-Forsyth’s 20-year journey and the impact it continues to have on athletes and families throughout the community.

Zachary Steele. During the ceremony, a portion of Pilgrim Mill Road was officially designated as the “SPC Zachary Evan Steele Memorial Road.” The designated roadway extends from the intersection of Bronze Oak Way and Aquatic Circle to Pilgrim Lake Drive. items.title: Big Creek Greenway Improvement Project | April 2026 | On the Move
items.summary: Forsyth County Parks & Recreation continues to make progress on the Big Creek Greenway renovation, a long-term project focused on enhancing safety, durability and the overall experience for Greenway users. In this latest edition of On the Move, Parks & Recreation Director Kirk Franz and Capital Projects Director John Jefferson share where the project stands today, why improvements are necessary and what residents can expect moving forward.

items.title: Site Selection & Conducting County Business | Freedom Park Campus FAQ
items.summary: Forsyth County's Freedom Park Campus will soon be home to over a dozen departments and roughly 335 employees. Learn more at www.forsythco.com/freedompark.

items.title: Employee Center & Increasing Efficiency | Freedom Park Campus FAQ
items.summary: The 42-acre County Administration Campus at Freedom Park will consolidate 17 separate departments into a single location, significantly improving the customer experience for citizens doing business with the County. The Freedom Commons employee center will provide opportunities for employees to enhance total health and will differentiate Forsyth County from surrounding counties as the best place to work while also decreasing the County’s total employee health insurance medical costs. items.title: Future Growth | Freedom Park Campus FAQ
items.summary: Forsyth County's Freedom Park administration building is designed with the future in mind as it stands ready to expand an additional 75,000 square feet and add a multi-level parking deck without the need for acquiring additional property or interfering with ongoing County operations. Learn more at www.forsythco.com/freedompark.

items.title: Mental Health Facility | Freedom Park Campus FAQ
items.summary: In part 3 of this video series about Forsyth County's Freedom Park Campus, County Manager David McKee discusses formerly proposed plans to include a mental health facility on the administration campus and the Board of Commissioners' decision to allocate funds toward an existing water & sewer infrastructure project. To learn more about Freedom Park, visit www.forsythco.com/freedompark.

items.title: Funding | Freedom Park Campus FAQ
items.summary: The Freedom Park administration campus is opening to the public soon! In the first of a five-part series, Forsyth County Manager David McKee discusses the funding sources for the project, which will consolidate 17 separate departments into a single location. Learn more about the new campus at www.forsythco.com/freedompark.

items.title: Friends Cumming Grill receives U grade in Aug. 4 health inspection
items.summary: Friends Cumming Grill received a U grade with a score of 42 in an Aug. 4 routine inspection. The public report lists violations involving food protection, temperatures, sanitation, facility maintenance and pest control, and says the facility voluntarily closed pending compliance and reinspection.

items.title: Forsyth County plans tennis and pickleball court improvements at three parks
items.summary: Four new tennis courts are planned at Sawnee Mountain Park, while courts at Matt Community Park and Coal Mountain Park are scheduled for resurfacing. The county says some disruption is expected, but construction dates, costs, and closure schedules have not yet been published.
